title: Legal forms directory and questionnaire

questions.label: Do you plan to attend any appointments by video or other telehealth?
Do you want to use electronic intake and the patient portal rather than request paper forms?
Will someone other than the patient sign or make treatment decisions for the patient?
Do you want to authorize a specific release of ordinary health records to another person or organization?
Has the office asked you to complete a consent for protected records from an outside substance-use treatment program?
Has the office asked you about a separate release of specially protected substance-use counseling notes?
Do you want to discuss a separate release of specially protected psychotherapy notes?

forms.section: Consent to Counseling and Informed Treatment
forms.when: Discuss and document informed consent before relevant nonemergency treatment; a request for discussion requires follow-up.
forms.positive: Yes, I consent to outpatient counseling
forms.why: Explains the therapy, risks, benefits, alternatives and confidentiality limits. Discuss and sign before routine therapy; you may request discussion before consenting.

forms.section: Financial Agreement and Good Faith Estimate
forms.when: Review financial terms with all patients. An individualized Good Faith Estimate applies when required for uninsured/self-pay care; this acknowledgment is not the estimate.
forms.why: Explains session-day payment, disclosed fees and the 24-hour cancellation policy. Review before the first session. Ask the office about your specific amount and any required Good Faith Estimate.

forms.when: Provide the notice and make a good-faith acknowledgment effort. A patient may decline acknowledgment without being denied care for that reason.
forms.why: Explains how information is used, shared and protected and describes your rights. Everyone receives it. A signature is requested, but you may decline acknowledgment without being denied care for that reason.

forms.section: Patient attestation and consent to submit
forms.when: Final intent and accuracy attestation for online intake. It does not replace any separately required consent.
forms.why: Records accuracy and your intent to submit this online intake. Sign for online submission after reviewing your answers; it is not permission for optional releases.

forms.when: Use before telehealth when the patient chooses remote services; no telehealth signature is required for in-person-only care.
forms.why: Explains remote-treatment risks and procedures. A separate consent is needed before telehealth; in-person-only patients need not sign it.

forms.when: Obtain agreement for electronic workflow; keep individual contact-channel choices separate and offer a paper alternative.
forms.positive: I agree to electronic intake and portal use
forms.why: Explains electronic intake, portal and signature choices. Agree only if choosing this workflow; a paper alternative is available. Individual contact preferences remain separate.

forms.when: Complete when someone acts for a patient. The office must review actual authority and applicable minor-consent rules.
forms.why: Identifies a person acting for the patient and the claimed authority. The office must verify capacity, court documents and applicable minor rules; age or family relationship alone does not establish authority.

forms.when: Use for a chosen disclosure requiring authorization. A No choice requires no signature and does not itself bar care.
forms.why: Totally optional for routine therapy. Use only for a specific desired disclosure that requires authorization; it excludes specially protected notes. A No or blank choice is not permission.

forms.section: Optional consent for Part 2 substance-use records
forms.category: Not routine — conditional outside Part 2 records
forms.when: Indian Creek reports it is not a Part 2 program. Not required for routine intake; use only after office review of applicable outside protected records. A blank or No choice gives no authorization.
forms.why: Not routine: Indian Creek is not a Part 2 program. Use only after office review of applicable protected outside records. Reporting substance use alone does not make this necessary.

forms.section: Separate consent for SUD counseling notes
forms.category: Not routine — conditional outside Part 2 records
forms.when: Indian Creek reports it is not a Part 2 program. Not required for routine intake; use only after office review of applicable outside protected records. A blank or No choice gives no authorization.
forms.why: Not routine. Separate optional consent only when applicable protected substance-use counseling notes are involved; office review is needed.

forms.when: Only for specially protected psychotherapy notes, independently of ordinary progress records and general releases.
forms.why: Totally optional for routine therapy. Applies only to specially protected psychotherapy notes, which are different from ordinary progress notes. Any authorization must be specific and separate.

statement: This is a form guide, not consent, a signature, a legal determination or permission to disclose. Unanswered or uncertain situations need office review. You may open any form; a form is never signed automatically.
